grammar.explanation: After a verb's connecting form, this pattern describes an action or change continuing and developing over time.
Attach this pattern to a verb's negative stem to express an obligation: must or have to.
After a dictionary-form verb, this pattern expresses a change into a new situation or behavior: come to do something.
After a plain-form clause, this pattern reports information heard from another source: it is said that or apparently.
With a volitional verb form, this pattern expresses thinking of doing something or intending to do it.
After a dictionary-form verb, this pattern states the purpose of an action: in order to.
After a verb's connecting form, this pattern emphasizes completion and can convey regret about an unwanted result.
After a plain-form clause, this pattern reports an accepted or commonly repeated claim: it is said that.
Used as an invitation, this pattern proposes doing an action together: let's do something.
This pattern names a prominent example before referring to other members of the same group: including or starting with.
This pattern reports information learned from another source, meaning it is said that or apparently. It follows a complete plain-form clause.
This pattern means even and emphasizes an unexpected or extreme example. With a negative predicate, it can mean not even.
This pattern gives the cause of a following result, meaning because or due to. Here it explains why the present buildings date from after the war.
This pattern expresses the purpose of an intentional action, meaning in order to.

grammar.explanation: This pattern expresses an uncertain possibility, meaning may or might. The polite ending keeps the same meaning.
This pattern introduces a supposition, meaning if we take it that or assuming that. Here it sets up a comparison between two districts.
This pattern describes the extent or degree of something, meaning to the point that. Here the number of shops is so large that they cannot all be counted.
This pattern means to try doing something to see what it is like. It also appears in suggestions, requests, and invitations.
This pattern introduces a representative example from a larger group, meaning including or starting with.
This pattern follows a dictionary-form verb and expresses the ability or opportunity to perform that action.
This pattern marks an action or change as completed, often with a feeling of regret or an unwanted result.
This pattern expresses an uncertain possibility, meaning may or might.
This pattern marks something as a point of comparison. Here it means in contrast to.
This pattern reports information learned from another source, meaning reportedly or it is said that.
This pattern follows a dictionary-form verb and states that an action is planned or scheduled.
This pattern identifies the role or category in which something is considered, meaning as.
This pattern lists representative activities without implying that the list is exhaustive.
This pattern describes something as having the qualities typical of the preceding noun.
This pattern attaches to a verb stem and means that the action is easy to do.
This pattern indicates that the state resulting from an action remains unchanged during another action.
This pattern joins two actions performed at the same time by the same subject, meaning while.
